{{< include /knowledge/includes/setup-parameters.qmd >}}

The human brain is 200,000 years old, living in a world that's 200 years old, making decisions that will kill a person in 20 years.

This is not a bug. It's a feature. A terrible, murderous, diabetes-inducing feature.

## The Selfish Gene and Cognitive Limitations (It Was a Good Idea at the Time)

Richard Dawkins put it perfectly: ["We are survival machines, robot vehicles blindly programmed to preserve the selfish molecules known as genes."](../references.qmd#selfish-gene-dawkins)

Translation: Humans are biological vessels controlled by chemicals that want to make more chemicals.

Genes don't care if a person is happy. They don't care if a person lives past 30. They care about exactly one thing: making copies of themselves before something with teeth finds the host.

For 99.9% of human history, this was brilliant. Now it's why the population is fat, anxious, funding nuclear weapons, and slowly developing diabetes while their teeth fall out.

## Part 1: The Brain Was Optimized for a World That Doesn't Exist

### The Scarcity Brain (Or: Why Humans Cannot Stop Eating)

For 200,000 years, calories were rare. Finding a beehive wasn't "prediabetes in a tree"; it was the difference between children surviving winter or becoming the skinny corpses archaeologists find later.

So evolution programmed humans with one simple rule: **When calories are found, eat ALL of them RIGHT NOW before the hyenas show up.**

Fast forward to 2025:

- Modern humans live within walking distance of 14 restaurants selling 3,800-calorie meals
- Each meal contains [twice the daily calorie needs](../references.qmd#food-abundance-stats)
- The ancient brain still screams: "EAT EVERYTHING! WINTER IS COMING!"
- Winter never comes. Diabetes does.

The exact same brain that kept ancestors alive by gorging on mammoth fat is now killing people with fast food. Evolution doesn't do software updates (it's like still using Windows 95 to run nuclear power plants, technically functional, but nobody should be comfortable with this).

### The Violence Module (Or: Why Society Prioritizes Weaponry)

Fun fact: [15-30% of ancestors died from violence](../references.qmd#prehistoric-violence-rates). Not disease. Not starvation. Other humans smashing their heads with rocks over who gets the good berry bush.

The tribes that survived weren't the peaceful, loving ones. They were the paranoid, murderous ones who:

- Assumed every stranger wanted to kill them (statistically accurate)
- Struck first when threatened (natural selection at work)
- Formed tight combat groups to kill other combat groups (teamwork!)
- Hoarded weapons obsessively (can never have too many pointy sticks)

The human brain is still running this exact software. That's why:

- Humanity spends {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} annually on weapons likely never to be used
- People instinctively distrust those who don't look like their tribe
- Online arguments feel like actual combat (the amygdala can't tell the difference)
- Countries with [10,000 nuclear weapons](../references.qmd#world-warheads) are worried they don't have enough

The violence module that kept ancestors from getting clubbed to death is now building weapons that can end all life on Earth. This is what computer scientists call "feature creep."

### The Tribal Brain: Why Democracy Struggles with Scale

[Dunbar's number](../references.qmd#dunbar-number) says humans can maintain stable relationships with about 150 people. That's it. That's the social circle.

For 200,000 years, this worked great:

- The tribe had 150 people
- Everyone knew everyone personally
- Decisions affected people one could see
- Free riders got kicked out or starved

Now people live in a democracy with 335 million strangers where:

- Citizens vote for people they have never met
- To make decisions about people they will never see
- Using tax money that feels imaginary
- To solve problems the brain literally cannot comprehend

The brain treats anything outside the 150-person circle as an abstraction. That's why:

- People care more about a neighbor's barking dog than 10,000 people dying of malaria (the dog is RIGHT THERE being loud, malaria is just a concept with numbers attached)
- Local corruption makes people angrier than trillion-dollar Pentagon waste (the local guy stole $10,000 one can imagine, the Pentagon lost $2.5 trillion which is just syllables)
- People will donate to save one sick child but ignore statistics about millions (one child has a face, millions is just a very big number that makes the brain hurt)
- Democracy feels broken (because it requires superhuman empathy the primate brain literally cannot produce)

## Part 2: Genetic Slavery is Literally Killing Us

### Mortality Through Success

[Evolution prepared us for scarcity, predators, and violence](../references.qmd#evolutionary-mismatch). Humans got abundance, safety, and streaming video. Human bodies are experiencing the biological equivalent of "ERROR: SUCCESS NOT FOUND":

| What Evolution Prepared For | What Society Got | Result |
|-------------------------|------------|--------|
| Starvation | Unlimited calories | [42.4% obesity rate](../references.qmd#obesity-epidemic-stats) |
| Constant physical threats | Office chairs | Anxiety disorders |
| 30-year lifespan | 80-year lifespan | Bodies that fall apart at 40 |
| Small tribes | Global society | Constant existential dread |
| Clear immediate dangers | Abstract future risks | Complete inability to plan |
| Scarce mates | Dating apps | Paralysis from too much choice |

Genes succeeded spectacularly. They made billions of copies. They won evolution.

Individuals are just the disposable biological vessels they used to do it, and now people are confused why they can't stop eating processed snacks at 2 AM.

### Living in an Illogical Era

Here's the cosmic joke: Humanity has never been safer, healthier, or more prosperous. And society has never been closer to accidentally ending everything.

Humanity solved all the hard problems, then immediately invented new, awful problems to replace them. It's like watching someone win the lottery, then use the money to buy a tiger that eats them.

#### Solved Problems

- ✅ Starvation (society discards 40% of food because storing it is inconvenient)
- ✅ Predators (humans hunted them into extinction, then put them in zoos so children could see what was killed)
- ✅ Infant mortality (basically eradicated in developed countries, which makes the death rate in poor countries feel more optional and thus more tragic)
- ✅ Most infectious diseases (vaccines work despite what social media says)
- ✅ Dying at 30 (now people complain about turning 40, which ancestors would consider a miraculous lifespan worth celebrating daily)

**New Anthropogenic Problems:**

- ❌ Nuclear weapons (enough to [end civilization 20 times](../appendix/nuclear-weapon-cost-and-casualties-academic.qmd) because once wasn't enough)
- ❌ Climate change (humanity is terraforming its only planet by accident)
- ❌ Antibiotic resistance ([10 million deaths annually by 2050](../references.qmd#amr-10m-2050) because people gave antibiotics to cows)
- ❌ AI that might become sentient and decide humans are the problem (the AI would be correct, this is the risk of building things smarter than oneself)
- ❌ Social media (voluntary psychological torture paid for with attention)

Humanity resembles toddlers who found the nuclear launch codes. Godlike technological power, hamster-level impulse control.

## Part 3: Why Willpower is Insufficient

### The Brain is Not a Friend

People love to say "just make better choices." These people are misguided.

[The conscious mind, the part reading this, controls maybe 5% of decisions](../references.qmd#conscious-vs-unconscious-decisions-5-pct). The other 95% is the ancient lizard brain running software older than agriculture.

One cannot "choose" to not crave sugar any more than one can "choose" to not feel pain when stabbed. These systems run thoroughly deep.

When an individual sees a donut, here's what happens:

1. **Ancient brain**: "CALORIES! EAT NOW! SURVIVAL!"
2. **Modern brain**: "I should eat healthy."
3. **Ancient brain**: "SHUT UP! WINTER IS COMING!"
4. **Modern brain**: "But I'm trying to lose..."
5. **The Individual**: [Eats the donut]

The ancient brain always wins. It has 200,000 years of practice.

### Institutional Instincts

The same thing happens at the civilization level.

When politicians allocate budgets:

1. **Lizard brain**: "DANGER! BUILD WEAPONS! ENEMY TRIBES!"
2. **Rational brain**: "We should fund medical research."
3. **Lizard brain**: "WEAPONS! NOW! OR EVERYONE DIES!"
4. **Rational brain**: "But cancer is more likely to..."
5. **Congress**: [Adds $50 billion to military budget]

This isn't corruption. It's evolution.

The fear of violent death is older than language. The fear of slow death from disease? The brain literally cannot process it the same way.

That's why humanity spent {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} on weapons while [cancer research got pocket change](../references.qmd#global-cancer-research-spending).

## Part 4: The Prison Society Built

### Voting for Primates in Suits

Democracy asks the stone-age brain to make civilization-level decisions. It goes exactly as well as expected (badly, the answer is badly).

Citizens vote based on:

- Who looks stronger (alpha male bias, the brain thinks the election is a wrestling match)
- Who the tribe likes (social proof, if the clan approves, must be good)
- Who makes them feel safe (fear sells better than policy ever will)
- Who they'd have a beer with (relevance: zero, but the brain insists this matters for nuclear policy decisions)

They don't vote based on:

- Complex policy analysis (too many words, brain hurts)
- Long-term thinking (the brain stops caring after next winter)
- Statistical reality (numbers are abstract, feelings are real)
- Actual competence (boring, where's the tribal signaling?)

Society elects leaders using the same brain circuits ancestors used to pick the guy with the biggest club.

### The Military-Industrial Complex and Psychology

The brain's fear center (amygdala) is directly connected to the voting finger. Politicians know this.

Say "terrorism" and the lizard brain overrides everything:

- [More people die from falling out of bed than terrorism](../references.qmd#furniture-accidents-vs-terrorism-deaths)
- Individuals are [1,000x more likely to die from heart disease](../references.qmd#death-causes-vs-fear)
- But terrorism *feels* scarier

So humans spend trillions on military operations against threats that barely exist while ignoring the diseases actually killing them.

It's not a conspiracy. It's just evolution doing what evolution does: optimizing for the wrong thing.

## Part 5: Breaking the Chains

Every individual, from the most powerful president to the lowliest citizen, is doomed to a life of gradually escalating suffering until it ends in catastrophe.

All are prisoners to this flawed system. This system made sense in a world of scarcity when humans were hitting each other with rocks over the last berry bush. Kill or be killed. Hoard or starve. Trust no one outside the tribe.

But now? Humanity lives in a world of abundance and nuclear weapons. Society can feed everyone twice over, but would rather burn grain to keep prices high. Science can cure diseases, but the market would rather sell treatments forever (cured customers don't come back, bad for quarterly earnings). The software running human civilization is 10,000 years out of date, and the bugs are literally killing people.

Why doesn't society update the software? Why do humans cling to a system designed for cave-dwelling murderers when they could be an advanced civilization?

Because the current system makes inefficiency more profitable.

Every bomb makes someone rich. Every missile funds a yacht. Every war creates a billionaire.

Disease is profitable too. Not curing it, treating it. Insulin costs [$300 a vial](../references.qmd#insulin-history-and-pricing) because dead diabetics don't buy insulin, but cured diabetics don't either. So the system keeps them barely alive. It's good business.

The people making money from war and disease aren't evil. They just like money. One can't change human nature, but one can create economic systems that make curing people more profitable than killing them.

## Part 6: Breaking Free from the Programming

### The First Step: Acknowledging Biological Limitations

Humans are not broken. They are just running software designed for a different operating system.

The brain evolved to:

- Live 30 years (not 80)
- Feed 5 people (not think about billions)
- Avoid tigers (not understand statistics)
- Survive winter (not plan for retirement)
- Fight neighboring tribes (not prevent nuclear war)

Expecting the brain to naturally make good modern decisions is like expecting a cat to do taxes. The hardware just isn't there.

### The Solution: Leveraging Evolutionary Psychology

One can't fight 200,000 years of evolution. But one can hack it.

That's what a [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd) does. Instead of asking people to be rational (impossible), it uses irrational impulses against them:

- **Greed**: Make curing disease more profitable than building bombs
- **Fear**: Make politicians more scared of voters than lobbyists
- **Tribalism**: Create an us-vs-disease tribe instead of us-vs-them
- **Social proof**: Get {{< var global_population_activism_threshold_pct >}} participation so everyone else follows
- **Immediate rewards**: Pay people cash to join medical trials

This isn't trying to change human nature. It is using human nature against itself.

### Cognitive Awareness

Genes have enslaved humans in awful brains, but they also provided the ability to see the prison.

No other animal can think: "Wow, my instincts are maladaptive." That's uniquely human.

Humans are the only species on the planet that can:

1. Recognize they are badly programmed (self-awareness of bugs is step one)
2. Design systems to work around bad programming (debug without access to source code)
3. Use awful impulses for smart outcomes (redirect, don't resist)

Society can't change its nature. But it can build systems that make the worst impulses produce good results.

## The Cognitive Mismatch

The human brain is a 200,000-year-old piece of software running on hardware that hasn't been updated since the invention of agriculture.

It drives humans to:

- Eat everything in sight (hello, diabetes)
- Hoard resources forever (hello, billionaires)
- Fear everyone different (hello, racism)
- Build weapons obsessively (hello, nuclear arsenal)
- Ignore long-term problems (hello, climate change)

This same brain is now in charge of nuclear weapons, genetic engineering, and artificial intelligence.

What could possibly go wrong?

The same evolution that made humans short-sighted also made them smart enough to notice they are short-sighted. And if they are smart enough to see the prison, they are smart enough to escape it.

Society just has to stop pretending it is rational and start building systems that work with human fallibility instead of against it.

A [1% treaty](../solution/1-percent-treaty-academic.qmd) is that system. It doesn't ask humans to be better. It just redirects their worst impulses toward not dying.
